title: To The Yield
description:
Duel with friends, guards, and people that really piss you off.

Starting a duel. Ask an NPC to duel, or an NPC may challenge you. A box asks you to confirm:
Fight starts the duel.
Refuse declines, and the NPC hears that you turned them down.
Refuse silently declines without telling the NPC.
No box, no duel. The confirm box is the only sign a duel has really started and that you're both protected. If an NPC agrees but no box appears, the duel didn't start: don't attack them, ask again.
Yielding. Sheathe your weapon for about 4 seconds. The NPC can also concede on their own.
Nobody dies. Your opponent kneels when beaten. You drop at zero health and they stop attacking. Afterwards, whoever went down gets back up with some health.
A duel also ends if you walk away, never draw your weapon, someone outside the duel attacks either of you, or 3 minutes pass. Your followers are kept out of it.
Friends can duel you; followers need dismissing first. A current follower won't fight you (their follower status stops it), so dismiss them, then duel. If an opponent still won't actually fight (stays out of combat for about 4 seconds), the duel is called off instead of dragging on.
You can't duel while either of you is already in combat or on horseback, against someone hostile to you, or with a child. Your opponent has to be close by.

With SevActions 4.60 or highter, you can duel followers, freindly NPCs will duel each other, followers can duel each other

Notes: Heavily made by Claude, only tested by me. Only one of those things should give you confidence
author: whyregister
changelog:
0.8.0
- When your opponent yields, you answer: accept it, keep fighting, or make it a duel to the death (confirmed first; not offered against essential NPCs or your companion).
- A killing in a duel to the death is murder. set TTY_SanctionedDeath to 1 keeps it off your vanilla bounty; a SeverActions guard who sees it can still charge you, so you'll have to talk your way out of it.
- NPC duels: the winner answers a yield in their own words (accept, fight on, or ask for a fight to the death). You're asked about a fight to the death first: Allow, Stop it, or Stop it silently. Nobody dies without your say.
- Duels are now "with weapons and magic", and the prompts no longer tell NPCs what a duel means.
- Fix: an NPC answering another NPC's challenge could start a duel with you instead.
- Fix: the yield page could come up without its text.
